clue.text: Idiot gets another comradely tip: "Communication unbecoming to office"

parts.note: a twit is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: another says the letters of comradely tip are made into a different version of themselves

explanation.surface: A fool receives yet another piece of friendly advice, quoted as a slogan about unseemly behaviour in high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges the twelve letters of the phrase after the idiot. The definition wryly describes a president conducting foreign affairs by tweet, as in early 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: Conducting statecraft through brash social-media posts is widely seen as beneath the dignity of high office.

clue.text: Are endlessly having dust-ups over taxes

indicators.note: over says the quarrels lie across the trimmed word, enclosing it

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels or squabbles

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter of the word Are

explanation.surface: People are forever squabbling about tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final letter of 'Are'; 'over' has the quarrels wrapped round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: These are duties or levies charged, especially on imports, so they are a kind of tax.

clue.text: Dinosaur droppings inside, one assumes

indicators.note: inside says the droppings sit within the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to don clothes is to put them on, or assume them
guano is bird or bat droppings

explanation.surface: A guess about the fossilised dung found within a dinosaur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the droppings between the numeral and the verb for putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This large herbivorous reptile of the Cretaceous was one of the first prehistoric creatures ever named.

clue.text: Loony left vote destroyed respected leader

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ballot from the hard left has brought down an admired head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loony' rearranges L plus VOTE DESTROYED.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-sixth US president is honoured on Mount Rushmore, a sign of lasting esteem.

clue.text: Robin and Batman initially arrested — crazy!

indicators.note: crazy says the letters are scrambled wildly
initially takes just the opening letter of Batman

explanation.surface: Batman's sidekick and the caped crusader himself are locked up, which is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin' suggests Batman's partner, but here it is the bird; 'crazy' mixes B with ARRESTED.
explanation.definitionFit: This old name for the robin refers to the bird's orange-red chest plumage.

clue.text: Respected leader's call … h'm … with ban on air travel?

indicators.note: travel suggests these letters go on a journey and come back rearranged

explanation.surface: A revered leader's appeal, with a hesitant hum, for a prohibition on flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel?' rearranges the letters that follow the definition; the 's after 'leader' is just 'is' linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth US president is among the most admired leaders in American history, matching the puzzle's theme of presidents.

clue.text: Try leader out — that's more than enough!

indicators.note: leader out says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to sample food is to try it

explanation.surface: An exasperated call to give the boss the boot, since enough is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader out' drops the S from SAMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plentiful supply is generous, more than sufficient for the need.

clue.text: See 3
Pick up top off that bottle!

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: top off that takes the uppermost letter of that, the first in a down clue

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift a bottle and remove its cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage or nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean courage or nerve, bottle being informal British usage.

clue.text: The boss has spoken of Boris previously

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister, the boss of government, when the puzzle appeared
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister has spoken about Boris Johnson's past.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, later Prime Minister, previously ran London as its elected civic head.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson led London's city government from 2008 to 2016, so his former post was a civic one.

clue.text: Leaving government crushed like a ball

indicators.note: leaving government says the abbreviation for government, a single letter, departs from the word

parts.note: coffee beans that are crushed are ground

explanation.surface: Someone quitting office feels squashed flat, like a deflated ball.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the standard abbreviation for government.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is spherical, so describing something as shaped like one means circular or spherical.

clue.text: See 1
Elaborate on payment royal received, though not personally involved

parts.note: something elaborate or ornate is fancy

indicators.note: received says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone expounds on a fee the monarch was paid, while claiming no personal stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the two parts; 'received' puts R inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unattached and free of romantic or emotional ties means having no personal involvement.

clue.text: Compound at Calais is about to be reinstated

parts.note: in French, spoken at Calais, 'is' is est

indicators.note: reinstated read as re-instated says the word for about is put back in reverse

parts.note: re is Latin for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A chemical compound in a French port is about to be brought back into use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reinstated' read as re-instated turns the Latin word for about round, after the French verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically, these substances are compounds formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Parties (some) withdrawing — case dismissed

indicators.note: withdrawing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some litigants pull out of a lawsuit, so the judge throws the case out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks SEDIS from 'caSE DISmissed' and 'withdrawing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In a lawsuit or negotiation the opposing parties are the two camps or factions.

clue.text: Nice old leader is upset, having to entertain a jerk

indicators.note: to entertain is to take guests in, so one piece holds the other
upset in a down clue turns the letters over so they read upwards

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, is the national leader
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A former leader is distressed at having to host an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city but means pleasant; 'upset' makes SIMPO and 'to entertain' puts the jerk with its article inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone congenial and likeable is agreeable, the Italian and Spanish loanword meaning friendly.

clue.text: Article describing America in hell — horrible picture

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing a line round, says one piece goes around the other
horrible suggests the letters of in hell are mangled

explanation.surface: A news item portrays the United States as an inferno in a ghastly image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges IN HELL to NIEHLL, and 'describing' wraps it round A, after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is an informal word for a film, and this is Woody Allen's 1977 romantic comedy.

clue.text: Want to be noticed taking small lady up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole is read from bottom to top
taking says the noticed word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: to be noticed is to be seen
Enid is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A craving for attention, carrying a little woman aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts the small lady after the first letter of the noticed word, making SSENIDEEN, and 'up' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of poverty or lack is a state of deprivation.

clue.text: A less respected leader about to embrace flighty type — counteragent?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece encloses the other
about says the president's name is turned round

parts.note: Richard Nixon, who resigned over Watergate, is a US president held in lower esteem
a tit is a small bird, a flying creature

explanation.surface: A disgraced president is about to hug a fickle person, perhaps as an antidote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives NOXIN, and 'to embrace' puts the bird inside, after A. 'Less respected' contrasts with the themed respected leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: An antibody that neutralises a poison is a substance acting against another agent.

clue.text: Men atone finally for wrong … in small measure

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are put together incorrectly, in a jumbled order
finally takes only the closing letter of the word for

explanation.surface: Men at last make amends for their wrongdoing, though only in a small way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'for'; 'wrong' shuffles it with MEN ATONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit is one billionth of a metre, a tiny length used in physics and chemistry.

clue.text: Lead offered by 6, not 3

parts.note: the letters of the word lead are those of deal rearranged, so lead is a freshly arranged deal

explanation.surface: A lead given by one numbered entry rather than another.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'new' shuffles DEAL into LEAD. The programme was Franklin Roosevelt's (6), not Teddy's (3).
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D. Roosevelt launched this 1930s economic recovery programme; his cousin Theodore did not.

clue.text: Computers do it best — time you invested

indicators.note: invested says these letters are clothed inside another word

parts.note: to top something is to best it
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A boast that computers perform best, with a nod to the time someone put into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computers' are the people or machines that compute, and what they do is add up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To compute a sum is to add numbers up, which is exactly the phrasal verb here.

clue.text: Awkward at the start — new dude in secretary's private area

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the assistant's letters

parts.note: PA, a personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: awkward says the letters sit clumsily and are rearranged
at the start takes the opening letter of the word new

explanation.surface: A clumsy newcomer strays into the secretary's personal office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' shuffles the first letter of 'new' with the dude to make UDEND, and 'in' puts it inside the secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin term for the external genitals literally means parts to be ashamed of.

clue.text: Got Georgia's dosh

parts.note: to have won something is to have got it
GA is the postal abbreviation of the US state Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone has laid hands on Georgia's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the answer and 'dosh' are British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British slang words for money or cash.

clue.text: Scottish town makes appearance in news

indicators.note: in puts the broadcast word between the two letters

parts.note: N is short for new, so news read as plural gives two Ns
to air is to be shown in public, as a programme makes its appearance

explanation.surface: A Scottish town shows up in the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is taken as plural 'new' (N), hence NN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland burgh on the Moray Firth, east of Inverness, is a town in Scotland.

clue.text: Hit back with an "alternative fact" — journalist turned away

parts.note: an 'alternative fact', a phrase from the 2017 US presidency, is a polite name for a falsehood

indicators.note: back says the word for hit is read in reverse

parts.note: to tan someone is to thrash them
ED, an editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A press spokesperson strikes back with a dubious claim, and a reporter leaves in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for hit, giving NAT, placed after the falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged or made hostile has been driven off, made to feel distant and unwelcome.

clue.text: Once more in range earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the cooker comes before the word in

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: Something happening one more time within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a British range cooker, a large heat-storing kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean one more time, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Cause to attack over records

indicators.note: over says the phrase is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: to set a dog on someone is to cause it to attack

explanation.surface: Someone incites an assault because of what was written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Written jottings or memos are records of what happened or was said.

clue.text: Remove main ingredients stopping choice

indicators.note: stopping, as a filling stops a hole, puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: choice and elite both describe the select best

indicators.note: ingredients are mixed together, so the letters of main are stirred up

explanation.surface: Taking out the chief components blocks your options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients' shuffles the printed word to MINA, and 'stopping' puts it inside the word for choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of something or take it out of contention is to get it removed.

clue.text: Stretch working group

parts.note: to stretch resources is to tax them
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A period of time spent in a team at work.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology this is any classification group of organisms, such as a species or genus.

clue.text: See 5
Woman with appeal in paper not available

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for appeal inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An attractive woman features in a newspaper but cannot be reached for comment.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid daily.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it stands for a woman, as in the biblical story.
